author: buchanan_robert
text:
We were not so far away, but all our lives seemed

To be at an end; I had never been up to that place before; it was too

Dark for me to make out anything: we sat down on some high rocks by a stream, and lay there talking till daylight came. We did not see any one come that night; yet when day broke we heard voices behind us, or rather from above. They spoke loudly as if they wished to hide themselves from us, and walked very quickly along the bank towards where we lay.

For there are other parents down in Heaven who call me Dad;

text: The Beach In the evening sun I sat on a beach. The sea was so close; it caressed my feet as if they were stones. It looked like a bright blue swimming pool but instead there was sand underneath me, soft warm grains covering my body. But even then I could feel its cool touch against my bare skin. My ears listened for seagulls and the wind blew softly in between my hair. A feeling of calmness spread all around me. "Our Mother Used To Walk Here..." by George MacDonald

George Macdonald (1824-1905) is one of Scotland's most famous novelists. His best known works are The Princess and the Goblin, and The Miraculous Journey of Edward Tulane. In this piece he uses poetic prose to help children imagine life before their birth, when all they know of the world comes through their parents.
